attributes.residual: THREE mechanisms, each named with its measured cause. (1) HOISTED SECOND FORMAT STRING. Retail computes lbl_80114724 BEFORE the branch (`lis r3,HA` at +0x28, `addi r0,r3,LO` at +0x3c) and spends it in the else arm as `mr r4,r0`; we compute the pair inside the else arm. Probe A's failure cause, read from the object: a second NAMED local is not the retail form -- MWCC gives altFormat its own long-lived home and then needs TWO extra register copies (`addi r4,r6,0` and `addi r3,r5,0` at +0x1c/+0x2c) to place both strings, costing +2. Retail has ONE variable that is REASSIGNED, not two variables. (2) ADDRESS-THEN-LOAD FOR THE MTAP STATUS. Probe B is structurally CORRECT -- it emits retail's exact `li r3,0 @lbl_80344610(EMB_SDA21)` + `lwz r3,0(r3)` -- but it is +1 on its own because it does not remove our surviving `mr`, described next. (3) THE SURVIVING `mr`, which is the real blocker. Retail materialises the first format string IN PLACE inside the prologue slack (`addi r4,r4,LO` at +0x10, before `stwu`); we materialise it after the prologue and out of place (`addi r0,r4,LO` then `mr r4,r0`), one instruction more. That extra `mr` is what makes probe B a net +1 instead of a net zero. NOTE THE SIBLING EVIDENCE: print_n_of_m in game/ui/screensaver.c has the SAME mechanism (retail hoists `addi r0,r8,LO(lbl_8011D568)` above `stwu`, we emit it after the prologue) and attempt.parked.print-n-of-m.20260830.v1 records that global-base initializer and declaration/lifetime forms could NOT move that materialisation across the prologue. That is transferable negative evidence and it is why the initializer-versus-statement spelling was not re-probed here.
